requirements.label: ECON 101: Principles of Economics I
requirements.hint: Economics prerequisite.

requirements.label: Psychology Prerequisite
requirements.hint: Choose 1 of: PSYCH 111, PSYCH 112, PSYCH 114, or PSYCH 115

requirements.label: Sociology Prerequisite
requirements.hint: Choose 1 of: SOC 100, SOC 102, SOC 195, or SOC 300

requirements.label: ORGSTUDY 305 & 310
requirements.hint: Both ORGSTUDY 305 (Inside Organizations) and ORGSTUDY 310 (Formal Organizations and Environments) required: minimum 2 courses and minimum 6 credits.

requirements.label: Quantitative Skills
requirements.hint: 1 course, minimum 3 credits. Approved options are SOC 210, STATS 206, STATS 250, STATS 280, and QMSS 201, per the OS Curriculum Sheet effective Fall 2025 on the Organizational Studies website (file OSCurricSheetforStdtsEffF25Portrt.pdf). Note from the sheet: if you have AP Stats credit (STATS 180), you lose that credit if you take STATS 250 or SOC 210.

requirements.label: Cluster A: Organizations & Individuals
requirements.hint: Minimum 2 courses and minimum 6 credits from the Cluster A (Orgs and Individuals) elective list, per the OS Curriculum Sheet effective Fall 2025 on the Organizational Studies website (file OSCurricSheetforStdtsEffF25Portrt.pdf). Courses marked A or B on the sheet appear in both cluster lists and count in either, student choice. ORGSTUDY 295, 395, 490, and 495 are variable topics courses whose cluster depends on the topic offered each term, and PSYCH 487 counts only for the Psych of Prejudice topic; confirm topics with the OS office. No more than 2 cluster courses across A, B, and C can be at the 200 level, and no more than 2 can be taken off the Ann Arbor campus. Courses not on the cluster lists may be petitioned with the OS advisor.

requirements.label: Cluster B: Organizations & Society
requirements.hint: Minimum 2 courses and minimum 6 credits from the Cluster B (Orgs and Society) elective list, per the OS Curriculum Sheet effective Fall 2025 on the Organizational Studies website (file OSCurricSheetforStdtsEffF25Portrt.pdf). Courses marked A or B on the sheet appear in both cluster lists and count in either, student choice. ORGSTUDY 295, 395, 490, and 495 are variable topics courses whose cluster depends on the topic offered each term; confirm topics with the OS office. No more than 2 cluster courses across A, B, and C can be at the 200 level, and no more than 2 can be taken off the Ann Arbor campus. Courses not on the cluster lists may be petitioned with the OS advisor.

requirements.label: Additional Cluster Courses (A, B, or C)
requirements.hint: Minimum 3 more courses and minimum 9 credits chosen from the Cluster A, B, or C lists. Cluster C is the Interest Cluster elective list; all three lists are per the OS Curriculum Sheet effective Fall 2025 on the Organizational Studies website (file OSCurricSheetforStdtsEffF25Portrt.pdf). The planner subtracts the 4 courses already used for Clusters A and B. Within the 7 total cluster courses: at least two 300 or 400 level ORGSTUDY courses taken on the Ann Arbor campus at 3 or more credits each, no more than 2 courses at the 200 level, and no more than 2 courses taken off the Ann Arbor campus. Courses not on the cluster lists may be petitioned with the OS advisor.

requirements.label: 2 Upper-Level ORGSTUDY Courses
requirements.hint: Minimum 2 ORGSTUDY courses at the 300/400 level, taken on the Ann Arbor campus, for a minimum of 3 credits each. May overlap with Cluster A/B/C requirements.

requirements.label: Senior Research Capstone
requirements.hint: Field Research: ORGSTUDY 410 required. Honors students take ORGSTUDY 497 and ORGSTUDY 498 instead.

requirements.label: Major Total Credits: 34
requirements.hint: Includes all courses used toward the major requirements, including cognates from other departments; does not include prerequisites. The planner matches ORGSTUDY courses. Residency: maximum 2 courses taken off the U-M Ann Arbor campus (study abroad courses count toward this limit, even through a U-M program).
